items.title: Show HN: Rename.Tools – Open-source bulk file renaming in the browser
items.contentSnippet:
Hi HN, I built Rename.Tools after needing to rename a large batch of images. This is something I only do occasionally, so I couldn’t justify buying dedicated software for it. The free tools I tried didn’t quite fit my needs either.
When I discovered the File System Access API, a browser-based tool felt like a natural fit: open a tab when I need it, rename my files locally, and close it when I’m done. No installation or account required.

items.title: Show HN: Talktome - let your AI Agent call you
items.contentSnippet:
I built TalkToMe, an open-source macOS app that lets an agent call you from its current session. You answer, talk, and hear its replies. The agent keeps its tools, files, and history.
It works with Codex (Tested extensively, quite smooth), Claude Code (not tested heavily), Hermes, and other agents that can run shell commands. You can use ElevenLabs or local models to power the conversation. It's really surreal to see your agent call you for something!
Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/i

items.title: Show HN: Corral kill every command your agent starts
items.contentSnippet:
This summer I got to intern on the backend of an AI agent and I noticed that it would run commands like tail -f or some random background jobs and exit without terminating any of these. I got curious and looked up how Claude Code handles stuff like this, and it turns out they have similar problems.
There are issues about background processes from the Bash tool not getting cleaned up when the session ends, and one where a timeout sends SIGTERM to the whole process group and ends up killing Claude

items.title: Show HN: LLMs Play Chicken in Realtime
items.contentSnippet:
Was curious how LLMs would play chicken without a clear reward matrix, and then took it a step further by allowing communication and realtime decision making.
Each LLM is in an independent loop, where each turn they are given the current speed and time to impact, as well as their historical latency. They can pre-plan moves to account for latency.
